reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it explains a payment-based Forsage X4 plan involving purchased smart contracts, participant payments, upline labels, and bringing another person onto the plan. The speaker encourages viewers to post and put effort into the plan while saying it will pay off, making the payment discussion an encouragement to participate rather than a neutral explanation.

citations.quote: You'll get paid .025 for level one, .05 for level two.
So don't wait around. Just make the post. Put a little bit of work into this and you'll see it pays off.
when you bring somebody on, if they come on at level five and you own level five
you get each of those that not just the .4 you get all of them
If it's on 3, 4, or 5, it's going to fill their 3, 4, or 5 bubble up and it's going to go ahead and pay them that amount for whatever level it is that it is.

opening.argument: Judge the payment language in context. The speaker calls X4 "more of a team plan kind of a lottery" and explains that an overflow placement keeps moving until it reaches a particular bubble. That is a description of a contingent process, not a claim that every participant receives a payment. The speaker also says payments "can" come through spillover without a referral, rather than saying they will. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether this is an explanation of how the system operates or a promise of returns.

citations.quote: under for size x4 it's more of a team plan kind of a lottery.
it will fill up somebody else's overflow bubble and then keep filling up people until it finds somebody that's on a bubble 3, 4, or 5.
So you can get those payments without referring anybody.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited level amounts explain what a placement pays under the speaker's account; they do not establish that a viewer will reach a paying placement. Likewise, the invitation to make a post is encouragement, but it does not erase the speaker's description of overflow and lottery placement. The opening treats a conditional account of payments as though it were an unconditional earnings claim.

citations.quote: You'll get paid .025 for level one, .05 for level two.
The first two will be overflow payments.
So don't wait around. Just make the post.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling part of the plan a lottery does not turn this into a risk warning. The speaker gives specific payment amounts, says bringing someone on at a level produces payments across levels, and urges viewers to post because the work will pay off. The defense's conditional wording does not account for that direct encouragement to recruit and expect payment.

citations.quote: when you bring somebody on, if they come on at level five and you own level five
you get each of those that not just the .4 you get all of them
So don't wait around. Just make the post. Put a little bit of work into this and you'll see it pays off.

opening.argument: This is structured as an operational walkthrough. The title promises an X4 bubbles explanation, and the speaker works through six bubbles, overflow, and the circumstances in which bubbles three, four, or five pay. The speaker refers to their own differently colored bubbles and closes by inviting questions. A careful judge should distinguish explaining a diagram and its payment rules from establishing that the video itself asks viewers to buy into the plan.

citations.quote: Ethereum Forsage x4 Bubbles Explained! US Version! Easy to follow!
You have six bubbles underneath each square.
So you can see I got different colored bubbles down in there.
let me know if you got any questions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening is right that the speaker describes bringing someone on and names payment amounts. Those are also the mechanics a walkthrough of this diagram would need to explain. Even the cited encouragement to post appears after an extended account of which referrals fill overflow bubbles and which placements pay. Its presence does not make every preceding explanation a solicitation.

citations.quote: when you bring somebody on, if they come on at level five and you own level five
On your Versage X4, you just filled your overflow bubbles on your first two referrals and now you're waiting for your dings for payments for spilover on level three, four, and five.
So don't wait around. Just make the post.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can also promote participation. Here the explanation tells viewers how their first two referrals affect their payment position, then explicitly urges them to post and promises the work will pay off. The title's educational framing and invitation for questions do not neutralize that recruitment advice.

citations.quote: On your Versage X4, you just filled your overflow bubbles on your first two referrals
So don't wait around. Just make the post. Put a little bit of work into this and you'll see it pays off. I promise.

opening.argument: The visible graphic identifies a purchased smart contract, while the speaker describes payments associated with referrals and placements. That supports reading the video as an explanation of a purchase and referral arrangement; it does not, by itself, show a request for credentials or a demonstrated loss of funds. The speaker even distinguishes payments obtainable through spillover from payments tied to one's own referrals. The evidence establishes how the speaker says this arrangement works, but the specific statements cited do not establish every element needed to conclude that the viewer is being deceived.

citations.quote: You can get them from getting spillover or you can get them from getting a referral yourself.
So you can get those payments without referring anybody.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a purchased contract, payment levels, and encouragement to post. It does not identify a credential request or show an actual transfer or loss by a viewer. The speaker also says some placements can pay through spillover without that person making a referral. Those omissions and that alternative payment path deserve weight before treating the described arrangement as necessarily deceptive.

citations.quote: So you can get those payments without referring anybody.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A credential request or documented victim loss is not needed to assess what this video promotes. The graphic shows a purchased smart contract with an upline and payment positions. The speaker links bringing someone onto owned levels to receiving multiple payments, then tells viewers to post and says it will pay off. Spillover is presented as another route to payment within the same recruitment-linked structure, not an ordinary product benefit.

you get each of those that not just the .4 you get all of them
Just make the post. Put a little bit of work into this and you'll see it pays off.
